plan: My goal is to maximize profit in the long run. Since this is a single-round game and I want to maximize my profit, I should bid aggressively. The problem states that "winning can never cost you more than the item is worth to you" and that I pay the second-highest bid. This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy, as it maximizes your expected utility regardless of what other bidders do. Therefore, I will bid my value.

My goal is to maximize profit. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding above my value is safe. To maximize my chances of winning when my value is high, I will bid slightly above my value. This ensures I win if I'm the highest bidder and my value is greater than the second-highest bid. Given my value is $34, I will bid $34.1 to secure the win if the second-highest bid is below $34.

My goal is to maximize long-term profit. Since this is the first and only round, I need to maximize profit for this round. My value is $10. The optimal strategy in a second-price auction is to bid my true value, as this maximizes my expected utility. Bidding above my value risks winning at a price higher than my value if the second-highest bid is also above my value, which is not possible in a second price auction. Bidding below my value risks losing out on a profitable win. Therefore, I will bid my true value.
